epic.title: Post-phase-1 mechanisms + cleanup: governor identity, spine channel, wired checks, backlog, MCP door
epic.body: Cut from the confirmed design spec of explorer run `explore-post-phase1` (confirmed by Tommy, 2026-08-03). Full body follows in an immediate edit (the adapter's command-line path cannot carry it on Windows).

issues.title: Governor: per-agent identity — re-key bindings to session_id#agentId so readings fire
issues.body:
Workstream A of the epic spec (see epic body, section A). The governor's binding key changes from bare `session_id` to `session_id#agentId`, using the per-subagent transcripts the harness writes at `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session_id>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl`. The parent keeps its bare key. This one re-key fixes both #383 symptoms: binding pileup (release can find its own entry) and everything-ambiguous gauge reads. The reading's consumer is the engine's live trip mechanic (it fired twice during the exploration run itself).

**First act — pre-build probe (recorded branch point):** inspect the real PostToolUse hook payload before building anything.
- Payload carries the subagent's own transcript path → the fix is roughly a one-line re-key; the matcher never ships.
- Payload carries the parent's path → lift the structured matcher from the prototype's `agent_identity.py` (~250 lines, no engine/hook imports; matches `tool_use.input.command`, never a prompt substring — prompt text is contaminated by verbatim dispatch, proven live in exc-6).
- Neither shape → stop and re-scope before building.
Record the probe outcome and selected branch in the work area.

**Build:**
- Capability probe: assert the harness is 2.1.220+ and writes per-subagent transcripts; on an older harness the governor reports its mode instead of silently writing nothing.
- Fail-closed invariant: an unresolved identity never binds and never writes a reading. No guessing.
- Sidechain filter inversion: every subagent transcript line is `isSidechain: true`; fix `docs/GAUGE_WRITER_HOOK.md` (filter inverts for subagents; field table gains `agentId`). The doc fix belongs to this workstream.
- Stale-binding sweep: one-time sweeper retires the 47 pre-migration bare-key bindings unconditionally (no liveness test applies by construction). Dry-run first with before-state recorded, then real run, then delete the script; the commit notes it existed.
- Identity resolution records its own duration in the gauge write, per-call budget 100ms (placeholder).

**Acceptance (one-shot live script, kept runnable, not CI-wired):** dispatch ≥2 subagents running visibly distinct commands; assert (1) each agent holds exactly one binding under its own key, (2) the parent's binding never accumulates, (3) each gauge carries that agent's own model and plausible fill (advancing fill asserted only on an agent kept busy long enough), (4) a terminal agent's key disappears on release, and (5) **a trip fires from a per-agent reading on the live run** — the spec's stated done-condition is not "readings appear" but "a trip fires from a per-agent reading on a live run"; this issue is not done until that is observed. The run also asserts which identity path it took (re-key vs matcher) so a silent fallback cannot pass. Separately: feed an unresolvable identity, assert nothing is written. If the matcher ships, one pinning test for the identical-command race before the fails-closed claim is accepted; if the re-key branch ships, the race cannot arise.

**Out of scope:** metrics methodology (parked; the governor is token-load's only customer), any new consumer beyond the live trip mechanic. Prototype lift source: `C:/Programs/.proto-exc6-governor-subagent-identity` @ 75f684c — once the lift lands, delete the worktree; the commit SHA keeps the code recoverable.

issues.title: Engine channel: de-duplicate the RAIL echo and render anchors/constraints in `current`
issues.body:
Workstream B of the epic spec (see epic body, section B). Two defects in the engine's `current` output, both found by exc-8's cold agents, both preconditions for any instruction relocation (workstream C) and for the MCP door's verbatim imperative pass-through (workstream F).

- **RAIL echo de-duplication:** the RAIL line echoes the full gate imperative word for word — an exact 2x, measured at `checklist_engine.py:229`. Fix: the RAIL keeps its rail message and points at the imperative instead of repeating it. Without this, relocation increases token load instead of saving it.
- **Render `anchors` and `constraints`:** gates carry these blocks but the engine never renders them into `current`; 5 of 5 cold agents hit this independently. Before building the renderer, inventory what the corpus's gates actually carry in those blocks — if vestigial, deleting the two fields is the smaller fix and is on the table. Otherwise `current` renders both blocks with the gate. (Bears on #393: treatment verification proves only that a skill loaded.)
- **The class, not just the instances:** add a completeness property test — enumerate the fields a gate may carry and assert every populated one appears in the projection. That catches the next forgotten field; a golden diff alone cannot.

**Acceptance (automated regression tests, land in the suite):** goldens written before the change so the diff asserts the intended delta; `current` contains the imperative exactly once; the completeness property holds. No live run needed.

**Recorded dependency:** echo removal is assumed behavior-neutral for compliance — a graded guess. C's end-of-tranche tracer runs against the post-B channel; a compliance drop there indicts B before it indicts the tranche.

issues.title: Relocate gate-specific instructions into the spine — first tranche: Commander execute + plan
issues.body:
Workstream C of the epic spec (see epic body, section C). Move gate-specific instruction text out of always-loaded role prose into the spine templates the engine pushes at each gate — selectively. First tranche: Commander's `execute` and `plan` gates, where 84% of the relocatable words concentrate (census: 54.2% of Commander's true always-loaded words are gate-specific; `commander-core.md` is 57% gate-specific; `SKILL.md` is already 100% kernel).

**Ordering invariant: workstream B lands first, both fixes.** Otherwise relocation doubles its own payload and relocated constraints stay invisible.

- **What relocates:** paragraph-level units the exc-8 census classified gate-specific, into the gate's imperative in `COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json`. The census (single-rater, hand classification over 97 units, reproducible with the prototype's census script) is the selection authority, with one guard: a second independent classification pass covers the tranche units before they move, and a relocated unit must not be referenced by any other gate. No new judgment calls beyond that check.
- **What never relocates:** the bootstrap floor (instantiate-and-claim text cannot ride the channel it creates — hard, proven boundary); role identity, spine-use triggers, project-focus prose; rules spanning more than one gate; reference-on-demand text.
- **Per relocated unit:** a render assertion (text appears in `current` at its gate) and a named observable behavior a tracer can look for. The tranche takes no more units than have named observables (traceability cap).
- **End of tranche, once:** the exc-8 two-arm cold-agent tracer, n=3 per arm; pass = 3/3 instruction-arm runs perform the named behaviors, 0/3 no-instruction runs do (n and threshold placeholder). This is also the first bulk dose-response data point.
- **Cost accounting, per run:** measure `current` fire-frequency per gate on a real run first; the acceptance measure is total delivered tokens per run (relocated text is paid per `current` call; always-loaded prose once). Shrink target: `commander-core.md` always-loaded word count drops ≥40% (placeholder). If per-run tokens grow, either B regressed or the tranche is too big.

**Testing split (per spec):** C's acceptance runs — the tracer and the token measurements — are one-shot live evidence kept as runnable scripts, not CI-wired.

**Out of scope:** other roles; bulk relocation beyond the tranche (dose-response deferred); cross-role text. If implementation drifts toward relocating across roles, revise the spec first. Prototype lift source: `C:/Programs/.proto-exc8-spine-instructions` @ 5a283ad — once the tranche lands, delete the worktree; the commit SHA keeps the code recoverable.

issues.title: Wire the prose-only invariants: #329 worktree isolation + #328's two record()-survey invariants
issues.body:
Workstream D of the epic spec (see epic body, section D). Convert the highest-consequence prose-only invariants into wired, mechanical checks — the K1 "built-but-not-delivered" pattern (umbrella #345), worst instances only.

- **#329:** `verify_worktree_isolation.py` exists and exits with codes, but only prose invokes it — no spine template calls it (`grep -rln` returns nothing), while the corpus calls that failure "data loss, not friction." Wire it as a command-check precondition in every template whose runs enter worktrees. Because "every template" is the same omission shape that caused the defect, ship an enumeration check with it: a script lists worktree-entering templates and asserts each carries the precondition, so a template left out is a test failure, not a silent gap.
- **#328:** two invariants documented as mechanically enforced are wired as `record()` surveys — they store whatever the agent types and invoke nothing. Rewire as command checks; each conversion names its command and failure condition at build time. If no command can decide an invariant, it routes to the named-human bin instead — the two-bin rule (doctrine B0.3) cuts both ways.

**Acceptance (automated, land in the suite):** verify each converted check by re-running the command that failed; break the invariant deliberately in a scratch run and assert the engine refuses. A check that still passes once its guard is deleted has the #392 shape and fails review.

**Boundary:** the rest of cluster K1 (#243, #257, #280, #281, #288, #291, #313, #330, #344, #363, #373) consolidates into the cluster-level item in workstream E — this issue ships only the two conversions above. Tranche selection ranked by stated consequence (data loss beats contradiction beats drift), graded placeholder until something bites.

issues.title: Backlog consolidation + closeout debts — batched confirms, evidence on every close
issues.hitl_reason: Every close and consolidation executes only on Tommy's explicit confirm — batched, not one-by-one. The pre-authorized close class (both review passes agreed + evidence attached) still needs his one batch confirm, and cluster boundaries are his call; reverting them after closes means re-splitting a cluster item.
issues.body:
Workstream E of the epic spec (see epic body, section E). Mechanical tracker work; consolidation re-files work, it does not retire it — keep a count of real work items alongside the issue count, which relabeling cannot move.

- **Already executed (2026-08-03, approved):** the 12 adjudicated disagreements — closed #239, #244, #296, #336, #337, #338, #347, #349, #364, #374; closed #278 as duplicate of #409; rescoped #208. Backlog went 127 → 117.
- **Uncontested close candidates, awaiting batch confirm:** #131, #285, #289, #298, #322. Both passes agreed done/superseded/empty; each close carries its evidence in a comment. #298's verification = each of its 12 dispositions' evidence links resolves; #322 gets its settings.json wiring pointer noted before close.
- **Cluster consolidation:** re-file surviving in-the-weeds singles as cluster-level items per the K1–K13 map, excluding what this epic consumes (K2 → workstream A; the K1 tranche → workstream D). Before any single is absorbed, snapshot its body into the work area; each cluster issue links the singles it absorbs before those singles close.
- **Closeout-debt filings:** file as real issues — the unowned resolved-load-manifest finding (precondition of any kernel-and-fragment split, currently recorded nowhere but a closeout artifact); #308's unmet consolidation clause (exc-1 proved a migration was substituted for the required consolidation); the B1 first consolidation; the episode-store harvest. Parked debts get owners and a place to reopen from.
- **Done-condition, checkable:** every surviving open issue carries a label tying it to a target-architecture stratum or a reproduced defect, verified by one `gh issue list` sweep. "About a dozen real work items plus genuine standalones" is the expected shape, not the test.
- **Closeout check:** when this epic closes, compare what shipped against each workstream's stated obligation in the spec — the #308 failure shape, guarded by construction this time. Wave constraint: this check is the epic's terminal act — it runs only after every other issue in the epic lands, even though E's tracker work may execute earlier.

**Not touched:** episode contents (a K10/B1 question, carried open); unmerged branches including #264's three commits (needs #412's orphan-risk read, carried). Derive every count claim from `gh issue list` commands, never memory. Falsified by any close without evidence or any cluster item that does not link its absorbed singles.

issues.title: MCP front door for the engine — ~7 typed tools wrapping the dispatch loop
issues.body:
Workstream F of the epic spec (see epic body, section F). The engine gains a second front door: an MCP server exposing the drive loop as about seven tools — status, lease (claim/release), start, attest, advance, halt (block/resume), survey result (record/consolidate); paired verbs merge behind an `action` argument (the seven-over-eighteen grouping is a placeholder). The server wraps the engine's own dispatch function — no engine logic duplicated, so refusals, recovery hints, rails, and the journal ride through unchanged. The CLI door stays for hooks, headless/cron runs, and non-MCP harnesses; every uncovered verb keeps a documented CLI fallback. This is a deliberate first-round implementation: good-enough now over better later; the seam cleaves responsibility — problems using the engine land behind the MCP interface, problems building contextual inputs land before it.

**Tommy's four rulings (2026-08-03) are design constraints:**
1. Each agent gets its own server instance — one server holds one session identity and one bound spine; a parent and its subagent never share a lease identity; a status call always returns the caller's own context reading.
2. The schema cost is accepted: ~1,000 always-loaded tokens buy removal of invocation strings from 7 of 21 spine-template imperatives and most of the on-demand engine reference (~4,500 tokens, exc-9 measurement). The net always-loaded delta across C and F together is a measured acceptance number: on the instrumented run it must come out smaller than before.
3. Tool descriptions may be rich — teaching text in a description is just-in-time delivery. Channel boundary rule: a tool description teaches how to call that tool; a gate imperative carries what to do at the gate; instruction text lives in exactly one home. The bare-descriptions control arm is skipped by this ruling; trimming is a later item.
4. The governor lands behind the MCP: advisory and trip ride tool results as the primary channel for MCP-driven agents. F reuses workstream A's identity settlement (`session_id#agentId`) — the agent id is server-instance state and doubles as ruling 1's separation key. One identity mechanism, two consumers.

**Pre-build branch point (recorded):** does an interactive session pick up a fresh `.mcp.json` without a restart? Picked up → project-scope `.mcp.json` suffices (ships with the repo; settings.json is never touched). Not picked up → per-dispatch config generation is the delivery path and gets designed first.

**Acceptance (one-shot live scripts, kept runnable):** (1) rerun the exc-9 tracer protocol against a real role spine through the production door — a cold agent reaches done with zero malformed calls; (2) separation: parent + subagent drive two different spines simultaneously through their own instances; leases never collide, each status call returns its own reading; (3) inheritance fail-closed — dispatch a subagent with no special configuration and assert refusal or no-identity, never silently serving the parent's lease or reading (the failure exc-9 actually observed); (4) same-gate equivalence: CLI projection and MCP tool result carry the same imperative text, so the doors cannot drift.

**Depends on:** A (identity settlement), B (verbatim imperative pass-through of the fixed channel), C (ruling 2's net always-loaded delta spans C and F together — the joint number can only be measured with C's tranche landed). **Open question, recorded not settled:** whether C's end-of-tranche tracer must also re-run through the production MCP door is answered nowhere in the spec; the same-gate equivalence test covers door divergence of the imperative text, but not tracer re-execution. Surface this at build rather than deciding it silently.

**Out of scope:** description trimming, the bare-descriptions control arm, a gitlab-style third door, concurrency beyond the two-instance separation test. Prototype lift source: `C:/Programs/.proto-exc9-mcp-front-door` @ de6a084 — once the lift lands, delete the worktree; the commit SHA keeps the code recoverable. Known engine defects found by exc-9 (#315-shape cwd, refusals-counter zero) are filed via the triage issue, not fixed here.

issues.title: File the explorer run's triage-candidate defects
issues.body:
The confirmed spec's Out of scope section lists triage candidates from the explore-post-phase1 run itself, routed to filing at the route gate. Each candidate ends up either as a new issue or as a comment on its existing issue, linked back to the spec of record (`.agent-work/archive/2026-08-03-explore-post-phase1/DESIGN_SPEC.md`).

**New issues to file:**
- Engine refusals counter records zero when refusals happen before the lease claim (found by exc-9, reproduced).
- `verify_spec_confirmed.py --phase review` is unpassable by construction on a template-conformant draft: the standalone `UNCONFIRMED` marker check runs in any phase, but the marker may only come off at confirm. Found live this run — the review-phase check can never pass while the template's own marker is in place.
- `file_issue_set.py`'s github adapter passes issue bodies as a command-line argument (`gh issue create --body <text>`), which fails with WinError 206 on Windows for any body over the ~32K command-line limit. Hit live while filing this very epic (41KB epic body). Fix shape: write the body to a temp file and pass `--body-file`.

**Comments/annotations on existing issues:**
- Stop-rail refresh-request blindness of the #235 shape: attaching the refresh-request does not unblock in-session; a genuine context refresh is required. The spec's Out of scope records three live hits; a fourth landed at the confirm seam after the spec text froze, recorded in the spine journal (confirm-gate block, evidence e-confirm-2, in the archived work area). Comment on the existing issue if open, else file new with the occurrences as evidence.
- #346 (`constellation-diagnose` registration defect): reproduced first-hand this run — note the reproduction.
- #290 (12 of 19 skills missing `invoker:` tags): still live — note re-confirmation.
- #315 (command checks run without a set working directory): confirmed independently by exc-9 — note the confirmation.

**Constraints:** this issue only creates issues and comments — it closes nothing (closes belong to workstream E under batched confirms). Precondition: confirm the executing agent has tracker-write clearance (`gh issue create`/`gh issue comment`) before the wave that runs this; commanders have historically lacked it.

**Acceptance:** one tracker ref per candidate (new issue or comment), each linking the spec's Out of scope section. Derive the "all candidates covered" claim from the list above, checked off one by one.
